newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul Stock Exchange to list two new firms.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul Stock Exchange to list two new firms.

text.p: The Istanbul Stock Exchange said it would list on Thursday partial shares of textile firm EGS Egeser Giyim Sanayi Ic ve Dis Ticaret AS and frozen food producer Apeks Dis Ticaret AS on the national market.
Per 1,000 lira nominal-valued share, Egeser will open at 11,500 lira and Apeks at 11,000 lira.
Both companies had floated part of their capitals in separate public offers last week.

Egeser which is part of textile and readywear producing and exporting group EGS, sold 130 billion lira nominal-valued shares to a total of 5,660 investors when raising its capital to 330 billion lira from previous 200 billion.

Offer manager Korfez Investment said 52 billion lira of the offer was bought by 10 foreign investors, another 52 billion by 5,524 domestic investors, 16.823 billion by 33 domestic institutions and 9.177 billion by 93 EGS group employees.
It said British-based Banque National de Paris Plc which bought 13 billion lira worth shares was among the foreigners.
The publicly sold shares to be listed on the Exchange, make up 39.4 percent of Egeser's 330 billion lira capital.

Egeser produces raw materials and semi-finished items for textile and readywear producers and exporters in and outside the EGS group. It aims to use income from the public offer in raising turnover and paying down debt to lower finance costs.
Apeks sold 55 billion lira nominal-valued shares to a total of 1,104 investors when raising its capital to 250 billion lira from previous 120 billion last week.

Offer manager Ekinciler Securities said 23.52 billion lira of the total offer was bought by 1,090 domestic investors, 30.68 billion lira by seven foreign investors and 800 million by seven domestic institutional investors.
It said Donaldson, Luftin & Jenrette Intl Ltd which bought 13 billion lira of the offer and Merrill Lynch Intl. which got 5.35 billion lira of shares were among the foreigners.
The publicly sold shares to be listed on the Exchange make up 22 percent of Apeks's 250 billion lira capital.
